payload.text: Director Vance — D5's intake-and-placement contribution to the pipeline: East Oakland's placements flow through our district intake and are counted; what I can commit to in writing is the handoff, and the handoff is the problem. D5's portion is documented on our side but the step that carries it into INIT-007's placement-gap analysis is still not published, so the analysis cannot show what East Oakland actually contributed. My ask is concrete: publish the analysis with East Oakland's intake and placement figures named as their own line, not folded into a citywide average, and give D5 and D3 a written date for the district-level breakdown. Until that record exists, I'm not signing on to anything that treats East Oakland's contribution as measured. File the date, then we'll talk about moving the pipeline.

Director Vance — the placement-gap analysis is a city workforce publication, not a district handout, and I won't pretend D5's office owns the publishing stamp. What I own is D5's side: East Oakland young people's intake and placement figures, gathered with the neighborhood organizations already doing the work, and I will deliver that contribution in a form the publishing office can actually use. So identify the office of record for the pipeline's placement-gap analysis and the format it needs, and I will file East Oakland's contribution against it this cycle — with the community organizations' names attached, not just a spreadsheet. If the publishing office can't be named, say so plainly, and I'll bring the gap into a public briefing myself rather than let silence stand in for a document.

facts: Masjid An-Nur Oakland: community grief gathering organized
Darrin Davis and Chief Montez put the badge on the pickleball court. First Youth Community Event is the Badge & Paddle Classic

The Darrin Davis Community Youth Events program announced its first event this cycle: the Badge & Paddle Pickleball Classic, a free doubles tournament in East Oakland that puts Oakland kids, neighborhood residents and OPD officers on the same court. Partners are drawn at random, so nobody plays with who they came with. A teenager from Deep East might get a beat officer, a grandmother from Fruitvale might get the Chief. Davis announced it alongside Chief Rafael Montez, and the pairing is the point. The two met three years ago through the A's community policing work, with ride-alongs, youth clinics and school visits in West Oakland and Fruitvale, and what started as PR became a real friendship. Davis majored in criminal justice at Ohio State, was made an honorary police captain in his hometown of Columbus in 2032, and keeps that badge in his locker next to his batting gloves. His line has always been "Baseball's what I do. Justice is what I believe." Davis framed the tournament as the opposite of a crisis response: a chance for people to meet officers on a Saturday when nothing is wrong, and for officers to meet the neighborhoods they patrol by first name. Responders from the Oakland Alternative Response Initiative have been invited to enter a team, putting OPD and the behavioral health crews on the same bracket. OPD is the program's sponsor with support from the A's and Oaks, and every event stays free. Open questions: does Montez actually play, which A's and Oaks players sign up, and does Davis keep the program going if his playing days are winding down at 32 after missing major time twice in three seasons?
Darrin Davis works with the Oakland Police and Rafael Montez on youth outreach programs in the city.

Darrin Davis and Rafael Montez annouce the start of the Darrin Davis Community Youth Events program that will be a city-wide outreach iniative to run various programs throughout the city. Entertainment, Workshops, Keynotes, etc, in an effort to bring Oakland youth together to focus on common goals to help the communties. The Oakland Police is spornsoring these events along with added support from the Oakland A's and Oaks. The events are said to be happening monthly throughout the city and will always be free of charge. More details to follow on schedule of events in the city
